Cone-Traced Supersampling (CTSS) is an efficient spatial antialiasing solution for Signed Distance Field (SDF) rendering that performs supersampling along the traced ray near surfaces with partial visibility [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that CTSS is an efficient spatial antialiasing solution for SDF rendering that performs supersampling along the traced ray near surfaces with partial visibility. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'we present cone-traced supersampling (CTSS), an efficient and robust spatial antialiasing solution... CTSS performs supersampling along the traced ray near surfaces with partial visibility'. All specific details in the claim are directly present in the provided text.

This confirms that the method involves evaluating cone intersections within the view frustum to identify these surfaces during the ray marching (tracing) process.

The technique was proposed to address the limitations of conventional supersampling and post-processing filters [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the proposed technique (CTSS) 'does not require casting additional rays per pixel or offline prefiltering' (addressing limitations of conventional supersampling) and 'does not produce undesirable blurriness and ghosting' (addressing limitations of post-processing filters). It also describes CTSS as a 'reliable practical alternative to conventional supersampling' with 'comparable antialiasing quality at significantly lower computational cost.'
